text: They circle each other for a few seconds, and then nobody is circling any more.
Nobody says anything. There isn't anything to say.
It's not elegant. It's two people rolling around in the mud trying to kill each other.
It's over faster than anyone would like.
The maths isn't complicated, but it's not finished yet either.
There's a moment where everyone realises how outnumbered someone is.
Someone puts their back to a tree, and everyone else spreads out.
Somebody shouts and then everyone is moving at once.
For a second the two groups face each other like it's a proper battle. Then it turns into a brawl.
It's chaos: too many people, too many blades, and nowhere near enough room.

{K} picks up a rock and brings it down on {V}'s head until {V} stops trying to get up.
{K} forces {V}'s face into the mud and kneels on {V.their} back until the struggling stops.
{K} gets behind {V} and breaks {V.their} neck with a sound everyone will remember.
{K} has no weapon, so {K} uses {K.their} teeth. {V} bleeds out from the throat. Nobody watching will sleep tonight.
{K} drives a knife up under {V}'s ribs and holds it there until {V} stops moving.
{K} opens {V}'s throat with one pass of the knife. {V} looks surprised, mostly.
{K} stabs {V} eleven times. Somebody in the Capitol counts.
{K} puts the knife into {V}'s eye and leaves it there.
{V} turns to run and {K} sinks the knife between {V.their} shoulder blades.
{K} runs {V} through with the spear and lifts {V.them} off {V.their} feet.

{K} spears {V} through the gut. It takes {V} a few minutes, and {V} spends them crawling.
{K} puts an arrow through {V}'s neck from across the clearing.
{K} hits {V} with three arrows in quick succession. The third one is unnecessary.
{K} fires an arrow into {V}'s chest from so close the fletching brushes {V.their} shirt.
{V} runs. {K} lets {V.them} get twenty metres, then shoots {V.them} in the back of the head.
{K} buries an axe in {V}'s shoulder, wrenches it free, and finishes it on the second swing.
{K} splits {V}'s head open with the axe like firewood.
{K} brings the axe down into {V}'s chest and has to put a foot on {V.them} to get it back.
{K} takes {V}'s leg off at the knee with the axe. {V} bleeds out before anyone thinks of a tourniquet. Nobody was going to.
{K} runs {V} through with the sword, all the way to the hilt.
{K} cuts {V} open from hip to shoulder in one long stroke.
{K} takes {V}'s head off with a single swing. The head rolls further than you'd think.
{V} parries twice. {K} doesn't need a third try.
{K} caves in {V}'s skull with the mace. It makes a noise like a dropped melon.
{K} swings the mace into {V}'s ribs, then into {V}'s head, then stops counting.
{K} hits {V} in the face with the mace. {V}'s own family wouldn't recognise {V.them} now.
{K} takes out {V}'s knees with the mace, and then, without hurrying, the rest of {V.them}.
{V} takes a spear through the thigh and keeps swinging anyway.
{K} slashes {V} across the forearm, deep enough to see something white.
{V} takes a blade in the side and doesn't notice until later.
An arrow from {K} catches {V} in the shoulder and stays there.
{V} limps away with one of {K}'s arrows sticking out of {V.their} calf.
{K}'s axe takes two of {V}'s fingers. {V} has eight left and intends to keep them.
{K} opens a long gash down {V}'s back.
{K} cracks several of {V}'s ribs with the mace. Breathing is optional now, and painful.
{V} takes a hit to the jaw and spits out a tooth.
{K} breaks {V}'s nose with a forehead.
{K} gouges at {V}'s eye. {V} keeps the eye, mostly.
{K}'s sword opens {V}'s cheek to the teeth.
{V} goes down with a leg that doesn't bend the right way any more.
{V} takes a blow to the head and spends the rest of the fight seeing two of everyone.
{V} is bleeding from somewhere, and {V} isn't sure where.
{V} breaks away and disappears into the {zone}.
{V} dives into the undergrowth and is gone.
{V} runs, and nobody bothers to chase {V.them}.
{V} throws a handful of dirt in someone's face and bolts.
{V} plays dead until everyone leaves, which works better than it has any right to.
{V} throws {V.themself} down a slope and rolls away out of reach.
{V} gets away by the simple trick of running faster than anyone else.
{V} screams so loudly everyone else flinches, and uses the moment to leave.
When it's over, {W} {W.is} still standing. Nobody would have bet on that.
Somewhere in the Capitol, a lot of money changes hands. {W} {W.has} just done the impossible.
{W} stand{W.s} there afterwards looking more surprised than anyone.
Numbers win. They usually do.
Afterwards, {W} go{W.es} through the packs without saying much.
{W} didn't even need to be that good. There were just more of them.
It could have gone either way. It went {W}'s way.
{W} sit{W.s} down afterwards and shake{W.s} for a while.
Then it's quiet in the {zone} again, except for the birds.
{W} wipe{W.s} the blood off on the grass and move{W.s} on.
Nobody gets the upper hand. Eventually both sides back away, panting, and go separate ways.
They fight until everyone is too tired to lift their arms, then limp off in opposite directions.
A noise in the trees spooks everyone at once, and both sides scatter.
Nobody's winning, and everyone can see it. They agree, without a word, to call it a draw.
It starts to pour, and everyone suddenly has somewhere better to be.
